primary_task: Guide a scientist through a conversation to pitch, troubleshoot or strategically evaluate a research problem (e.g. summarize their idea, ask follow-ups, assess risks) using the Fischbach & Walsh problem-choice framework.

requirements.name: user conversation (ask follow-up questions)
requirements.evidence: "Ask: **\"Tell me the short version of your idea (1-2 sentences).\"**" ; "Then ask for more detail"
requirements.basis: "ask_user": "ask the user a question (with options) and read the answer in the conversation"

requirements.name: bundled references/ files (01-intuition-pumps.md ... 09-meta-framework.md)
requirements.basis: "read": "read files in the working directory; search them by name pattern or content (glob, grep)" (the manifest does not say whether the skill's reference files are present; check the installed skill folder)

requirements.name: PubMed (pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov)
requirements.evidence: "Literature Integration - Use PubMed searches at strategic points for validation"
requirements.basis: "Network egress goes through an allow-list proxy: the package registries and hosts pypi (PyPI), npm, GitHub (github.com, api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com), Ubuntu (apt archives), NuGet and the Go module proxy are open; other hosts are refused (for example huggingface, Microsoft Learn and Azure, Cloudflare, Expo, Neon and NVIDIA)."

requirements.name: web search (literature lookup alternative)
requirements.evidence: "Use PubMed searches at strategic points for validation" (a design principle, not a numbered step)
requirements.basis: "web_search": "search the public web and read result snippets"

notes: The core work is conversational reasoning and writing done by the agent itself. PubMed searches appear only as a design principle ("at strategic points"), so I marked them not hard; direct fetches to PubMed are outside the egress allow-list, though web_search snippets could partially substitute. If PubMed were read as mandatory, PubMed egress would be unavailable and the verdict would be BLOCKED. Unknown: whether the references/ files are installed (they add guidance but are not needed to hold the conversation).
